Ribosomes are the smallest organelles and the only ones with no membrane. The mitochondrion and the chloroplast are semi-autonomous organelles surrounded by a double membrane. Each has its own circular DNA and 70S ribosomes and divides by itself, which supports the endosymbiotic theory (Lynn Margulis, 1967) that they arose from engulfed bacteria.

A biomolecule is any organic molecule made by a living cell. Ninety-nine per cent of the atoms in protoplasm are just four elements — carbon, hydrogen, oxygen and nitrogen — and they are assembled into four great families: carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.

In bryophytes the gametophyte is the dominant, independent, green phase and the sporophyte is small and permanently attached to it — the opposite of the situation in a fern or a flowering plant.

That single habit — absorptive heterotrophy — explains almost everything else about them. It explains the hypha, which is the ideal shape for penetrating a substrate and maximising surface area; it explains why fungi are the chief decomposers of the biosphere; and it explains why so many are parasites.

They are the first plants with a true root to anchor them and to absorb water from deep in the soil, instead of the rhizoids of a bryophyte. iv. The sporophyte is the dominant, independent generation; the aerial parts are covered with a cuticle and bear stomata, so water loss is controlled. v.

Leaves are of two kinds — green needles adapted to drought (thick cuticle, sunken stomata, hypodermis of sclerenchyma) and brown scale leaves. Xylem has tracheids but no vessels, and phloem has sieve cells but no companion cells (the exception is the order Gnetales, which does have vessels).
